whyUnassigned: The inspected products contain incompatible identity, role, profile, ownership, and permission boundaries. Assigning an owner before reconciliation would turn one legacy model into ecosystem law.
invariants: A person is not an authentication account.
An account is not a role, business, membership, or profile.
A business can exist without a currently authenticated owner.
Business ownership and staff access are explicit, auditable relationships.
A profile presents a subject but never becomes identity authority.
Roles and permissions are scoped and cannot be inferred from presentation labels.
Consent records include purpose, subject, scope, decision, provenance, and lifecycle.
Verification applies to one subject and claim and cannot be generalized from an unrelated approval.
Cross-product identity links are opaque, reversible, auditable, and never created from email coincidence alone.

riskRegister.finding: MealScout carries a TradeScout ID on a separate local user row, but no inspected reconciliation contract proves one-to-one identity, unlinking, conflict handling, or consent.
riskRegister.requiredProof: Link, unlink, collision, recovery, account-deletion, and audit behavior across both products.

riskRegister.finding: Product roles, business type, occupation, staff state, and administrative authority are represented in overlapping scalar and array fields.
riskRegister.requiredProof: A permission matrix derived from explicit memberships and grants, with denial tests for every privileged mutation.

riskRegister.finding: MealScout declares Facebook and Google access-token columns on users; encryption, expiry, rotation, revocation, and active use were not established by this inventory.
riskRegister.requiredProof: Runtime call-site audit and storage controls before retaining, moving, or deleting any token data.

riskRegister.finding: Generic and claim-specific verification flags coexist, creating a risk that one approval unlocks an unrelated capability.
riskRegister.requiredProof: Every protected action names the exact claim, evidence level, expiry, and authority it requires.

riskRegister.finding: TradeScout has first-class businesses but the inspected core model exposes direct owner linkage; MealScout staff membership is limited to restaurant-scoped businesses.
riskRegister.requiredProof: Owner, administrator, staff, delegate, transfer, revocation, and orphaned-business lifecycle tests.

migrationGates: Inventory live authentication providers, sessions, callbacks, and account-recovery paths in each product.
Reconcile person and account records without using email as silent identity proof.
Approve product-membership, business-membership, role, permission, and consent vocabulary.
Select the canonical owner only after its deletion, export, audit, tenant, and recovery boundaries are proven.
Introduce adapters and shadow reconciliation before changing any live login or authorization path.
Retire legacy role and identity fields only after every consumer and privileged mutation has migrated.
